newsitem.title: UK: UK to tighten merchant shipping pollution controls.
newsitem.headline: UK to tighten merchant shipping pollution controls.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday it was strengthening its powers to prevent and control marine pollution from merchant shipping and deal with questions of liability and compensation.
The measures will be included in a Merchant Shipping and Maritime Security Bill announced in Wednesday's Queen's Speech outlining the government's new legislative programme.

It said the bill would require ports to prepare waste management plans and increase fines for illegal waste discharge, as well as widening intervention powers to cover any significant pollution, not just pollution on a large scale as at present.

The bill will also authorise the creation of temporary exclusion zones at sea to allow safety zones around ships and structures on grounds of safety or pollution and introduce new measures to control the operation of sub-standard shipping.
It will seek enabling powers to charge shipowners for port control inspections and emergency response measures, and to provide for improved compensation payments to victims of marine pollution.

It will also seek powers to require shipowners calling in UK ports or operating in UK waters to have insurance or other financial securities to meet their third party liabilities. -- London newsroom 0171 542 7768
